d.t: A valley head created through glacial erosion and with a shape similar to an amphitheatre.
d.e: A fine glacier descends from Mount Longstaff. It has cut very deep and the walls stand at an angle of at least 50°. Otherwise, although there are many cwms on the lower ranges, the mountains themselves seem little carved.

d.t: A cubbyhole or similar hiding place.
d.e: In front of the pavement again stretched a flat patch of rusty ground, a sort of little platform in the side of the hill where the sagging drying-lines stood and a chickens' cwtch built of orange-boxes.
I am expecting the big man to come round the corner and give me a ‘cwtch’ as he has done beside countless rugby fields.

d.t: To hug, cuddle, embrace, or comfort.

d.e: A family are about to have a meal round the kitchen table, so the dog is told to go and “cwtch” in the corner, out of harm’s way.
